messages:
santiago: Thanks for the turnout today. Starting a short thread to capture infra Qs and follow-ups from the all-hands.

kevin: Can you confirm which regions get the new GPU inventory first? I missed that slide.

santiago: First wave: us-west-2 and eu-west-1 get the initial A100 racks (testing pool). Second wave targets us-east-1 and eu-central-1. APAC (ap-southeast-1) is planned but later, pending customs/lighting checks.

maya: Will the initial racks be labeled for Dedicated customers or join shared pools first?

santiago: They'll join labeled onboarding pools. We validate, run firmware/kernel updates, then mark for either shared-burst or dedicated per ops/sales requests. No automatic direct assignment to Dedicated.

tara: Autoscaler question 1: does burst behavior change with the new pools?

maya: We added a per-pool "burstable" flag. If set, that pool can temporarily accept 1.5-2x load for a short cooldown (configurable, default 90s). There's a tenant cap so single tenants can't monopolize burst capacity.

kevin: Any changes to preemption or queue ordering? Our long-running test jobs have been held up before.

maya: Preemption policy now has a soft window. Jobs <12s can take burst tokens; preemption for reserved tiers only triggers after queued >120s. We'll expose thresholds as config so teams can tune.

infra-bot: [deploy] autoscaler/v2 deployed to staging 2025-05-02T09:10Z.

santiago: Routing fallback update: routes now support per-tenant region blacklists and a graceful-degrade model that falls back to quantized variants when needed, but only if route opt-in is enabled.

tara: Is graceful-degrade on by default? Automated fallback concerns me for customer-facing routes.

maya: Not by default. It's opt-in per route. We'll gather sample quality metrics during canaries before considering default enablement.

kevin: Where can I find the canary schedule and validation checks?

santiago: Eng-platform will publish the canary doc today. Plan: 48-72h alpha canary in a single AZ, expand if no regressions. Validation: p95 token latency, cold-start counts, queue length, and sample quality tests.

ops: Action items noted:
- maya: land tenant_cap default and expose cooldown config (due 2025-05-15)
- eng-platform: publish canary runbook + schedule (due 2025-05-18)
- ops: confirm customs ETA for apac racks (due 2025-05-10)

kevin: Can we get a quick post when racks have tracking numbers so we can plan migrations?

santiago: I'll open a dedicated "rack-tracking" thread when vendor provides numbers. For planning, assume tentative May/June timelines, but treat them as soft.

infra-bot: [link] runbook draft: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/a100-canary-draft (access: eng-platform, eng-sre)

maya: If you have latency-sensitive routes, please list them in the runbook so we include them in targeted tests.

kevin: I'll add our gen-api and rerank services.

ops: We'll coordinate maintenance windows around the canary. Recommend avoiding major product deploys during canary windows.

santiago: Thanks all. Post any additional Qs here and we'll fold them into the canary checklist.
